One concrete mismatch: the LED-24 row says without condition that 'the outcome is the same whichever remittance is uploaded first, the netting PLB L6 before, between or with the PLB L6s paying that claim's interest'. ADR 0084 D5 says this holds only 'while the later payment is split by the same weights in either order or can reach no line'. The row leaves out that exception.

ADR 0084 D5's weight-change exception is untested. D5 covers a claim's lines changing weight between uploads (a later approval, or a recoupment of only some lines) around a netting take-back, and says the outcome then 'still errs low, never above the cash'. No LED-24 variant has that shape. The order-independence properties in packages/ledger/src/interest.test.ts use the same line specs and weights in both orders. So that sentence of the ADR is pinned by nothing.

ROI statements and period totals when a waiting payment is written later. A PLB L6 payment that waits and is written in a later pass is dated to the PLB L6's paid_on (effectiveOn: adjustment.paid_on, apps/worker/src/reconcile/remittances.ts ~1213). Period totals filter by effective_on (packages/ledger/src/totals.ts:155). The system's roi_statement for a period is stored once (apps/worker/src/reconcile/statements.ts:155-157, ON CONFLICT ... WHERE generated_by IS NULL DO NOTHING). So a statement generated while the payment waited leaves it out, the period's live 'Interest, net' later differs from that statement, and no later period's statement picks the payment up. The new waiting cases (twoChainsOutOfOrder, partlyTakenBackBetween, oneLineBetween, laterPaidAfterNetting) make these late, backdated writes routine. Neither the reviewers nor the ADR address this.

A specialist's adjustment of an interest entry (D8; the test at apps/worker/src/reconcile/interest.db.test.ts:763) has not been checked against the new paths. interestUnplaced, interestOutOfReach, the outOfReach cache and mayYetHold all read writtenOf, which holds entries keyed by their evidenceId (remittances.ts:1128-1131, 1052-1058). The Covered 'person actions' item handles reversing a claim match, reversing an interest match, matching by hand and reopening a written-off line. It does not cover a person lowering a payment entry, or correcting a take-back entry, of a PLB L6 that another PLB L6 still owes a take-back against. Nobody has worked out whether 'never above the cash' and order independence survive such a correction.

The CAS-42.3 at-size test (apps/worker/src/reconcile/reconcile.large.db.test.ts, extended in 8a6d0f26) does not guard F-M2-2's fix. The ADR records 33.7 s with the old per-take-back rebuild and 26.9 s with the fix, both well under PASS_BUDGET_MS of 150 s, so reverting the once-a-pass holdings leaves CI green. Its take-back phase also has no PLB L6 that nets a take-back against payments. As a result, payments that wait (re-walked on every pass for good, with outOfReachOf and unplacedOf) are never timed at size. The Covered items give only an analytic cost argument for these paths.
